name: Hyper-Kamiokande
summary: A next-generation Japanese underground water Cherenkov observatory will extend Kamioka’s accelerator, atmospheric, solar and supernova-neutrino programme with a much larger fiducial mass.
physics_targets: Leptonic CP violation with accelerator neutrinos
Atmospheric neutrino oscillations and mass ordering
detection_principle: High-sensitivity photomultipliers detect Cherenkov rings in a very large water tank. The detector will also serve as the far detector for a J-PARC beam programme.

sites.name: Japan; underground in the Kamioka area, Gifu Prefecture
sites.location: Japan; underground in the Kamioka area, Gifu Prefecture

status.label: Under construction
status.evidence: The official overview identifies Hyper-K as a project aiming to begin experimentation in 2028.

timeline.event: Official project overview aims to start observation in 2028.

collaboration.name: Hyper-Kamiokande Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Tank dimensions
key_parameters.value: Approximately 68 m diameter and 71 m height

key_parameters.name: Main photodetectors
key_parameters.value: Current construction configuration: approximately 20,000 50-cm PMTs and about 800 multi-PMT modules; the earlier design allowed up to 40,000 large photosensors.

results.summary: The collaboration reports detector construction and projected sensitivities; no Hyper-K neutrino-physics result is claimed before operation.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
